record.title: Sierra Leone COVID land-border closure and initial return window
record.scope: National land borders with Guinea and Liberia
record.direction: Land movement across both neighbouring frontiers; return window prevents an immediate absolute two-way interpretation.
record.movement: Ordinary cross-border movement and passenger travel.
record.exceptions: Essential commodities; temporary return window for people on the other side.
record.enforcement: Minister described controls at crossing points and custody for unauthorised entry; exact post-by-post enforcement is unverified.
record.consequences: ChildFund reported disruption to cross-border trade.
record.relationship: Distinct Sierra Leone health policy from Guinea’s later security closure W-007 and Liberia’s W-022 health order. Do not sum overlapping bilateral border-days.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.official_rationale: Prevent entry and spread of coronavirus.
record.context: Presidential order announced for midnight on 27 March; a subsequent ministerial explanation says the return window ended on 2 April.
record.uncertainty: 27 March is the formal order date, not proof all passage stopped that night. The Awoko page carries a later publication date but its body dates the briefing to 1 April. Retrospective July and September reopening narratives have different scopes; no universal endpoint selected. The original State House URL now returns unrelated content; fresh indexed official text and a contemporary report support the announcement. Midnight wording is retained as the stated 27 March formal date, without a precise operational timestamp.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Formal order 27 March; return window reportedly ended 2 April. Later reopening evidence is insufficiently precise and uniform for a duration.
